Messages.Author: Christopher Cates
Messages.Body:
A question came up yesterday that are group was quite divided on.  The
card Glaser Rounds says that it "can't be used the first time a gun is
used in a combat".  Half the group was arguing that since it the gun had
been used in a combat 6 turns ago that it "had been used in _a_ combat".
The other half were arguing that it was refering to a particular combat,
and that the gun had not not been used yet in this particular combat.

Just so things we pointed out do not get rehashed here, some of the
first group pointed out that other combat cards with round restrictions
state can't be used in the first round of combat, but that is countered
by pointing out that a gun doesn't have to be used the first round of
combat, so those card references are irrelevant.

End result was the group turned to me, since i'm on the net, but I have
no idea.  I can see this going either way.  We decided to flip a coin
(result: glaser rounds couldn't be used this combat until after the
gun was used this combat).

I respect net wisdom, but i think for this I'll need a WotC answer
to convince both sides of this argument.

Thanks,
Chris.
cat@wintermute.ucr.edu

Messages.Author: Tom Wylie
Messages.Body:
Christopher Cates <cat@wintermute.ucr.edu> wrote:
>A question came up yesterday that are group was quite divided on.  The
>card Glaser Rounds says that it "can't be used the first time a gun is
>used in a combat".  Half the group was arguing that since it the gun had
>been used in a combat 6 turns ago that it "had been used in _a_ combat".
>The other half were arguing that it was refering to a particular combat,
>and that the gun had not not been used yet in this particular combat.

The use of "a combat" means "any given combat".  You have to wait until
a gun's second strike during a given combat to use Glaser Rounds; you can't
use it in one combat, then use the rounds on its first strike in the
next combat.  Sorry for the ambiguous wording.
